name: PWE Undisputed Championship
epitaph: PWE's own top belt, and the only one it ever crowned in a ladder match. Four men climbed for it at New Years Resolution on 25 January 2003 and Scott Curtis came down with it, helped up the ramp afterwards by the president who had just knocked one of the other three through the ropes. Five days later Lynx put the champion's head through a vending machine backstage and asked for an inferno match for it at the next pay-per-view; the fed was still running a tournament for shots at it in April, and the answer to Lynx's question is not in the surviving record.

name: PWE Entertainment Championship
epitaph: Won in a Tables, Ladders and Chairs match at New Years Resolution by the fed's own president, against a man who had jumped him in a backstage room before the bell and was fired on the microphone for it while still lying in the ring. The president defended it on the Shockwave card of 13 February 2003 against Micheal Flash; whether he kept it is not in the surviving record.

name: PWE Hardcore Championship
epitaph: The third of the three belts PWE crowned in one night. Andre' Sanders beat Justice Paine for it at New Years Resolution on 25 January 2003 and was still listed its champion on the fed's own Champions page a fortnight later, with Walter Parker named his first contender.

name: PWE Tag Team Championship
notes: The fed's own Champions page of 13 February 2003 lists the belt with VACANT in the champion's row and a dash in both contender slots (/promotions/pwe-projectefed/archive/champions-2003-02.html); its own Tag Teams page, captured in July, is an empty table (tagteams.html). No reign of it survives.
epitaph: PWE hung a tag team championship on its own Champions page, put VACANT where the champions' names go, wrote a dash in both contender slots, and awarded it +7 points on its own point system for a win that the surviving record never records anybody having. Its own Tag Teams page was still empty in July 2003.
